Check: The numeric rules in the guide are common starting points - confirm exact limits with the shop that will make the part.
Every feature has a function. Anything that doesn’t is removed or simplified.
Part count has been reviewed. Combination opportunities are checked.
Standard materials, stock sizes and fasteners are used where possible.
The intended manufacturing process and volume are stated.
Tight tolerances apply only to functional features.
General tolerances cover everything else.
Surface finish requirements are no tighter than needed.
Datums are clear and reflect how the part is made and measured.
Internal corners have radii, ideally one common value.
Pocket and hole depths are within standard tool reach.
Walls are thick enough to avoid deflection.
Features can be reached with as few setups as possible.
Standard hole and thread sizes are used.
Bend radii, hole sizes and flange lengths follow the thickness rules above.
Holes are clear of edges and bend lines.
Bend relief is included where required.
Wall thickness is uniform or blends gradually.
Draft is on all relevant faces, with generous fillets.
Undercuts are avoided or justified.
A cost estimate exists, and the top cost drivers are identified.
Lead time and supplier capability are confirmed.
Inspection requirements are achievable and not excessive.
